Sevilla for Living

Your starting point in Seville

Finding a room, getting around, understanding paperwork, meeting people and discovering local life can feel overwhelming when you first arrive.

Sevilla for Living is an independent student-focused information project designed to help you navigate the practical side of the city and connect with the people, places and stories that make it what it is.

Everyday essentials

Practical guide

Our editorial guide is organised around the real questions students face when settling in Seville. Open a topic to see the starter information.

01 / HOUSING

Finding a place to live

What to check before choosing a room or signing a rental agreement.

Start by setting a realistic monthly budget, including utilities, transport and any agency fees. Ask whether the room is rented under a written agreement, what the deposit covers, which bills are included and how notice periods work. Never transfer money before verifying the property and the person offering it.

Our next editorial step: add a first-hand student checklist, local rental vocabulary and a reviewed list of tenant-support resources.
02 / TRANSPORT

Getting around

Understand the options for travelling between home, campus and the city.

Seville has urban buses, a metro line, tram services and cycling options. Your best choice depends on where you live and study. Compare routes and current fares before buying a pass, and check service updates when travelling late or during public holidays.

Our next editorial step: add a student-friendly route comparison and tips from people who commute to the main campuses.
03 / DOCUMENTS

Paperwork & appointments

A plain-language starting point for administrative procedures.

The steps depend on your nationality, length of stay and personal situation. EU citizens and non-EU students may follow different procedures. Identify which process applies to you before booking an appointment, prepare the required documents and rely on official information for current instructions.

Our next editorial step: publish separate explainers for EU registration, NIE-related questions and student residence procedures, reviewed against official guidance.
04 / UNIVERSITY

University life

Make the most of campus services and your international student network.

Save the contact details of your international office, check your academic calendar and ask about student cards, libraries, language support and associations. Joining a student group can make it easier to find practical advice and build a social circle.

Our next editorial step: add campus-specific information and student interviews.
05 / DAILY LIFE

Settling into a routine

Small practical steps that make a new city feel familiar.

Locate your nearest health centre, pharmacy, supermarket, laundry and essential services. Save useful addresses on your phone, learn the local emergency number and ask your university or residence team where to get help with everyday questions.

Our next editorial step: create a neighbourhood starter map with useful services checked by the team.
06 / SOCIAL LIFE

Meeting people

Find ways to connect beyond the classroom and tourist hotspots.

Look for language exchanges, student societies, volunteering opportunities, workshops and neighbourhood activities. Try returning to the same places and events: familiar faces and shared routines are often the beginning of friendships.

Our next editorial step: add a curated list of recurring meet-ups and student recommendations.
Editorial note: these are starter explainers for the MVP. The team can expand them with original reporting, interviews, photographs and verified local information. Administrative and legal requirements should always be checked against official sources.

Beyond the postcard

Local context

Understanding Seville means paying attention to its neighbourhoods, histories, traditions and the people who shape everyday life.

Neighbourhoods

Every area has its own rhythm

Triana, Macarena, Nervión, San Bernardo and the historic centre are not interchangeable backdrops. Each has its own stories, community networks, shops and relationship with the city.

  • Listen to the people who live there.
  • Support local businesses and markets.
  • Respect residential spaces and their everyday rhythms.
Culture & belonging

Culture is something we share

Local traditions carry historical, social and personal meanings. Approaching them with curiosity means learning their context, respecting different perspectives and taking part thoughtfully.

  • Ask before photographing people.
  • Learn about the history behind celebrations.
  • Explore contemporary culture as well as heritage.
Who we are

A local perspective.
An international outlook.

“A website to simplify, help and integrate.”

Sevilla for Living is a digital information and public-service project created for university students and young international people starting a new chapter in Seville.

Our mission is to make settling in easier through practical guidance, accessible journalism and local cultural context. We want to connect newcomers with the real city and the people who make it every day.

Our motto: “No seas un simple turista.” Don't just pass through. Get to know the place, listen to its people and become part of the city.
